subject: Milestone roadmap & credit triggers — AWS Marketplace offer (Meridian Logistics)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@meridianlogistics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:03:20 -0400
Subject: Milestone roadmap & credit triggers — AWS Marketplace offer (Meridian Logistics)

Hi Sam —

Great speaking earlier. As discussed, I sketched a short evaluation runway that ties credits and stepped discounts to milestone outcomes so Meridian can trial performance without upfront full commitment. High-level proposal attached (MAP-v1.xlsx). Key points: 

- Week 0–4: PO C kickoff / integration + small-scale POC (5k tokens/day). We provide a $10k evaluation credit in the AWS private offer to cover this period.
- Week 5–8: Expanded trial (50k tokens/day average) — if latency and throughput targets are met (95% requests < 300ms, observed with your 32k seq distribution), an additional $25k credit is released and we enable the 10% usage discount.
- Month 3–6: Ramp window — metrics-based commit band triggers. If monthly spend crosses $60k MRR-equivalent, auto-apply 18% committed discount and reserved capacity pool; otherwise maintain on-demand pricing with continued operational support.
- Fail-safe: If performance/regression shows repeat SLA misses for 7 consecutive days, automatic downgrade to a fallback VM pool and credits revert (we still provide SRE support to remediate).

We'd route the commercial steps through an AWS Private Offer so credits stitch into invoice and usage. I included a draft marketplace link for the private offer and an example DocuSign PO placeholder in the spreadsheet.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm milestone acceptance (Sam), 2) Redwood legal & procurement to review pricing bands (Marcus, Priyom), 3) We generate the AWS Private Offer draft and DocuSign PO for Meridian procurement.

Attaching: MAP-v1.xlsx (milestone schedule & credit ledger).

Thanks —
Jonas
VP, Cloud Sales

Thanks for the outline and for the call. A few quick clarifications before we loop procurement into formal PO discussions: 

1) On the $60k MRR trigger for the 18% discount — is that measured as 30-day rolling usage billed through AWS marketplace?
2) Are the evaluation credits non-recoverable (i.e., applicative only to usage within the private offer) or can we request a cash credit if AWS billing flows don't align?
3) What operational SLA do you guarantee for the ramp window (SLOs / credits for missed targets)?

Marcus / Priyom —

Looping you in — Sam had three quick clarifying questions (copied below). I drafted a proposed commercial mechanism that addresses the procurement concerns and keeps us protected operationally:

Draft commercial mechanics (proposed):
- Credit mechanics: All evaluation credits are applied as AWS marketplace private-offer credits tied to the offer ID; they reduce the first invoice(s) and are non-refundable cash-wise. This ensures credits reconcile on their billing statement and prevents out-of-band cash requests.
- Measurement window: 30-day rolling usage measured at AWS Marketplace billing granularity; pacing checks at day-30 and day-60 for commit triggers.
- SLA & remediation: 99% availability SLO for API endpoints during trial, with a 10% credit (of the then-current monthly invoice) for a rolling 7-day window of SLA breach beyond an alertable threshold.
- Discount bands (example): 0–$59,999 — on-demand; $60k–$149,999 — 18% committed; $150k+ — 25% committed + reserved capacity guarantee. Discounts require a signed Marketplace PO committing to a minimum 6-month runway (can be front-loaded as monthly commit or annual prepay).

Please review pricing bands and legal language. I attached a short PDF with proposed term language to send to Meridian procurement (pricing_terms_draft.pdf). If we agree, I'd like Marcus to greenlight the banding and Priyom to confirm legal ok.

Jonas

---
Attachment: pricing_terms_draft.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@meridianlogistics.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:22:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Milestone roadmap & credit triggers — AWS Marketplace offer (Meridian Logistics)

Jonas —

This looks sensible. A couple of suggestions to tighten risk and make it acceptable to finance: 

1) Make the $60k trigger a "soft commit" that elevates to a firm pricing discount only after Meridian executes a 6-month marketplace PO for the committed band. In other words, the trigger is an eligibility signal; the customer still signs to lock-in the discount for accounting.
2) Stagger the credit release: 40% on POC completion, 60% on trial expansion. That gives us better clawback leverage if the tech integration doesn't proceed.
3) Add a failover model clause: if we detect persistent misuse (automated scraping or batch spikes beyond agreed cadence), we reserve the right to throttle and pause credits pending remediation.

If Priyom confirms legal language, I approve the banding and we can push the private offer draft to Meridian procurement. I'll also ask finance to prepare the reserved capacity SKU proposals so we can show exact unit economics to Meridian.

Marcus
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
